newsitem.title: UK: Chamberlain Phipps bought out, says receiver.
newsitem.headline: Chamberlain Phipps bought out, says receiver.

text.p: One of the two joint receivers of footwear materials company Chamberlain Phipps said on Thursday that independent business consultant John Fallon had led and completed a buy-in/buy-out for the company along with some senior executives of the firm.

Arthur Andersen, the accountancy firm, and its two partners Murdoch McKillop and Simon Allport were appointed joint administrative receivers of the UK operations of Chamberlain Phipps after it became insolvent last year.
In a separate statement, Chamberlain said the businesses were sold for a "significant but undisclosed sum".

The management team's new company, named Chamberlain Phipps Materials Ltd had acquired the business and assets of the UK materials operations together with its Canadian, Hongkong and Indian subsidiaries.
"I am delighted that we have now completed this buy-out which preserves both the Chamberlain Phipps name and 250 jobs in the UK," John Fallon said.
Arthur Andersen said it and its partners had completed a "fundamental corporate restructuring" of the group that had helped to sell the businesses.

"A measure of the success of this restructuring and rescue is that it has been accomplished with relatively few redundancies (around 10 percent) and all the trading businesses now have a new future ahead of them," Arthur Andersen said.

Apart from Fallon, the management buy-out team consists of Roger Payne (deputy managing director and operations manager), Bill Irvine (finance director), Oscar Muto (sales and marketing director) and Malcom Bradshaw (vice president and general manager, Canada).
The team was backed by institutional funding with working capital from TSB Commercial Finance.
